record.paper_title: Offline Reinforcement Learning: Tutorial, Review, and Perspectives on Open Problems
record.context_brief: Calibrated Q-function uncertainty for offline dynamic programming
record.original_question: How can offline approximate dynamic-programming methods that use high-capacity function approximators such as deep neural networks obtain calibrated epistemic uncertainty estimates for Q-functions, so that the algorithm can identify untrustworthy out-of-distribution actions without becoming either overly conservative or overly loose?

evidence.quote: While such explicit uncertainty-based methods are conceptually attractive, it is often very hard to obtain calibrated uncertainty estimates to evaluate PD(Qˆπ) and Unc in practice, especially with modern high-capacity function approximators, such as deep neural networks.

In practice, imperfect uncertainty sets can give rise to either overly conservative estimates, which impedes learning, or overly loose estimates, which results in exploitation of out-of-distribution actions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a Markov decision process M = (S, A, P, r, γ) with state space S, action space A, transition kernel P(s' | s, a), reward function r(s, a), and discount factor γ ∈ [0, 1). Let π denote a policy and Q^π(s, a) := E_π[ Σ_{t≥0} γ^t r(s_t, a_t) | s_0 = s, a_0 = a ] its action-value function. In the offline (batch) setting, the learner is given only a fixed dataset D = {(s_i, a_i, r_i, s'_i)}_{i=1}^N drawn from some unknown behavior distribution μ(s, a) over S × A, and may not interact with M. Approximate dynamic programming methods produce an estimate Q̂(s, a; θ) using a high-capacity parametric function approximator (e.g., a deep neural network) by approximately solving the Bellman fixed-point equation on D.

For (s, a) outside the effective support of μ (out-of-distribution state–action pairs), Q̂(s, a) is generally unreliable. Uncertainty-aware offline algorithms attempt to use an epistemic uncertainty estimator Unc(s, a) and a posterior PD(Q̂^π) over Q-functions to penalize or filter such (s, a). Define Unc to be calibrated on D if there exist computable, data-driven functions L(s, a) and U(s, a) such that, for every policy π and every confidence level α ∈ (0, 1),

   Pr_{Q^π ~ posterior given D} [ L(s, a) ≤ Q^π(s, a) ≤ U(s, a) for all (s, a) ∈ S × A ] ≥ 1 − α,

with intervals tight enough that, when used inside an offline policy-improvement procedure π_{k+1} = arg max_π E_{s ~ d}[Q̂(s, π(s)) − β · Unc(s, π(s))] (or an equivalent constraint-based formulation), the resulting policy is neither (i) so conservative that it fails to improve over the behavior policy on in-distribution actions, nor (ii) so loose that it selects out-of-distribution actions whose true Q-values are arbitrarily lower than predicted.

Problem. Design an algorithm that, given only the offline dataset D and a deep-network-based Q-function class, produces such a calibrated epistemic uncertainty estimator Unc(s, a) (and corresponding bounds L, U) for Q^π and prove finite-sample guarantees of the form: with probability at least 1 − δ over D, the learned policy π̂ satisfies J(π̂) ≥ J(π*) − ε(N, δ, complexity of the function class, coverage properties of μ), where π* is the optimal policy on the support of μ, and ε → 0 as N → ∞ under stated coverage assumptions, while simultaneously avoiding exploitation of out-of-distribution actions.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a well-known open problem in offline reinforcement learning. While many approaches (bootstrapped ensembles, MC-dropout, Bayesian neural networks, conservative Q-learning, EDAC, SAC-N, MSG, and others) have been proposed since 2020 to approximate epistemic uncertainty for offline Q-learning, recent surveys and empirical studies continue to report that obtaining truly calibrated Q-uncertainty with deep function approximators remains unsolved: practical methods still trade off over-conservatism against OOD exploitation and lack tight finite-sample calibration guarantees. No published work has resolved the problem in its general form.

status_evidence.title: Offline Reinforcement Learning: Tutorial, Review, and Perspectives on Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Obtaining calibrated uncertainty estimates with high-capacity function approximators is highlighted as a major open challenge for offline ADP.
status_evidence.claim: The need for calibrated Q-uncertainty in offline RL is an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Uncertainty-Based Offline Reinforcement Learning with Diversified Q-Ensemble (EDAC)
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes diversified Q-ensembles to better approximate epistemic uncertainty in offline RL, but does not give calibration guarantees.
status_evidence.claim: Recent methods address the problem heuristically without producing provably calibrated uncertainty.

status_evidence.title: Why So Pessimistic? Estimating Uncertainties for Offline RL through Ensembles, and Why Their Independence Matters (MSG)
status_evidence.snippet: Shows that ensemble independence affects uncertainty quality and that current uncertainty estimates remain miscalibrated, often forcing a tradeoff between conservatism and OOD exploitation.
status_evidence.claim: Empirical evidence that calibrated Q-uncertainty for offline deep RL remains unresolved.
